brief: Day 1 of Q3 bank earnings (C, GS, JNJ, JPM, WFC) showed consumer spending and credit staying strong because the labor market keeps both up: card spend grew 10% YoY at JPM and 13% at C, while delinquencies and net credit losses fell YoY at C and WFC. JPM reflags its bullish consumer call from the October 12 Morning Briefing, citing Chase spending data showing September spending up 6.6% YoY, an acceleration from August's 5.3%, across all income cohorts, and sees Q3 earnings as a positive catalyst for Retail and Consumer Discretionary even though its JP2RTL basket is 8.7% off its August peak. Bank stocks C and WFC fell 5.6% and 3.1% despite in-line results; JPM's Rob O'Dwyer attributes the selloff to quant and passive flow given a flatter 2s10s curve, not fundamentals, and argues investors should fade the move and buy banks. Separately, AI and semis extended their slide while flows rotated into hyperscalers META, MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN, and JPM reiterates its Tactically Bullish US equity view into earnings, flagging a Momentum/Tech unwind and AI credit fears as the key risks.
